title: InstallUtil references a remote payload
description: Detects InstallUtil execution that references content over HTTP, HTTPS or FTP.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may use InstallUtil to retrieve or execute remote .NET content while proxying through a signed Microsoft binary.
hypothesis.rationale: MITRE documents InstallUtil proxy execution, SigmaHQ maintains a remote-download analytic using the same protocol markers, and Microsoft lists InstallUtil among applications that can bypass application-control policies if allowed.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify InstallUtil commands containing a remote HTTP, HTTPS or FTP reference while leaving local assembly installation, unrelated executables and incomplete commands unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Inspect the remote reference and .NET installer context; InstallUtil is legitimate but usually should not consume internet-hosted content directly.
steps: Review the complete command, URL, effective original filename, parent process, account and endpoint role.
Correlate the URL with network, file and .NET assembly activity, then inspect downloaded content, signer, hash and installer callbacks.
Confirm a documented development or deployment workflow; otherwise contain the endpoint and investigate the source and follow-on behavior.
false_positives: Approved .NET build, test or deployment workflows that intentionally pass a remote assembly or installer resource to InstallUtil

validation.expected_outcome: Match InstallUtil commands containing HTTP, HTTPS or FTP references; do not match local assemblies, unrelated processes or missing command lines.
